Inflation is only caused by the printing of more money without hard money (like gold or silver) backing it. Spending money does not cause inflation, except in one case: when the money-printers spend/loan money for it's first time being spent/loaned, entering it into circulation. The federal reserve can print all the money it wants and not cause any inflation, but only so long as they never put it into circulation. But the moment they loan the newly printed money to the federal government or spend it on something themselves, inflation occurs.

Inflation is only caused by the printing of more money without hard money (like gold or silver) backing it.

People keep reciting this rule and I wonder how it got so widely spread as the one and only rule, but there's really a lot more to it. First hit on a search already gave me quite an extended list of other reasons:

http://www.economicshelp.org/macroeconomics/inflation/causes-inflation/

The reason people keep "reciting this rule" is because it's reality. Inflation occurs when the supply of a fiat currency grows without an equal growth in the supply of hard money backing it. The result is more currency with less value per unit of currency. That is inflation. That's it. Any other attempt at defining it is a waste of time.

In fact, I would argue that any other explanation of the cause of inflation probably comes from someone who doesn't really know what inflation is.

It's complicated.

1) Rich people invest the vast majority of their wealth in illiquid assets. E.g. a billionaire would be likely to have less than 1% of their wealth in a liquid form (cash, bank accounts, etc). Thus they can't easily "spend it".

2) The greater the value of your illiquid assets, the longer it takes to liquidate (sell) them. The more people trying to liquidate at once, the harder it becomes. Remember the Housing Crash of 2008 where sellers were foreclosed upon because everyone was trying to liquidate their illiquid assets (houses) at once?

3) A mass spending spree would increase the velocity of money and thus increase inflation, but is highly improbable for reasons #1 and #2.

4) Could we confiscate the 1%'s wealth to pay for "Free govt gibs" like education and health? That's not how it works. Let's say you want to encrypt 20 gigs of data. What you will end up doing is creating a file that's 20 gigs in size. Once you do that, you assign two passwords to have two partitions in the encrypted file.

Partition A: Encrypted Porn. Partition B: Super secret stuff.

First you dump your porn into partition A, then you dump all of your super secret stuff into partition B. From this point on you NEVER touch partition A again (you can browse it and look at the porn, but you can't write any new data to it). If let's say the porn takes up 10 gigs and the super secret stuff is 5 gigs, that means you've used 15 gigs out of the 20. But partition A will allow you to use the full 20 gigs (while showing 10 gigs of free space), thus overwriting all your super secret stuff, and you lose all of your data.

So technically the fake encrypted partition A will allow you to use the full 20 gigs that you originally wanted to encrypt, but it will destroy the hidden stuff you didn't want anyone to see. Good if law enforcement screw up, bad if you shoot yourself in the foot.
Simple solution, have a login profile setup with an auto run wipe program. They get the login, and presto! No more data.
